items.title: South Central 94: Veeramani case, Reporter TV raid and ECI dissent
items.summary: How did allegations against a powerful mining baron remain buried for years, despite the police being alerted? In this week's South Central, hosts Dhanya Rajendran and Pooja Prasanna discuss the allegations surrounding Tamil Nadu mining baron Veeramani, the police investigation into the case, the raid on Reporter TV’s newsroom in Kerala and growing questions over dissent within the Election Commission of India. To discuss the first topic, the hosts are joined by TNM ’s Chennai Bureau chief Shabbir Ahmed to examine how allegations of sexual assault of minors involving Veeramani remained uninvestigated despite a complaint allegedly being made to senior Chennai police officials in November 2024. Shabir explains how the police later filed a closure report citing a lack of prosecutable evidence, only for a court to reject the report and order a reinvestigation. The discussion looks at the role of politicians, police officials and others who may have known about the allegations, and the questions raised by the police’s handling of the case. “According to the closure report, the final report that was filed by the CCB in the POCSO court, the police first came to know about this crime in October 2025. But now Ranjan Kumar, Congress leader, he has claimed that in fact, he knew about it in November 2024 and he had approached the top officials of Chennai police,” he says. The episode then turns to Kerala, where the police raid on Reporter TV ’s newsroom has sparked a debate over press freedom and media ownership. Senior journalist MG Radhakrishnan argues that entering the newsroom and taking journalists’ phones was unacceptable, while the discussion also examines Reporter TV ’s own record, the political affiliations and conduct of media owners, and the wider problem of corporate ownership and concentration in Indian media. “The kind of increasing hegemony of the corporate class in media, it actually has changed the entire media discourse in India. The particular corporate groups, which with interests in so many other business sectors telecom, energy, infrastructure, banking and all those getting into media definitely has created a lot of problems in India's media. The first casualty has been objectivity because there is a huge case of conflict of interest,” MG Radhakrishnan adds. items.summary: Days after The Indian Express investigation, the Election Commission’s decision to introduce an additional declaration for new voters applying through form 6 has come under fresh scrutiny, with two petitions filed in the Supreme Court and the Bombay High Court. The paper had reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections to several EC decisions, including changes to form 6. They had said these changes should have come after amendments to the Registration of Electors Rules. The paper had earlier reported that the ECINET portal had added a declaration asking new voters whether their names or that of their parents or grandparents existed in the last special intensive revision’s electoral roll. Advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi has filed a PIL before the Supreme Court PIL seeking the restoration of the original form 6 and an SIT probe into exclusion of voters – the court is set to hear it next week . Ratnagiri resident Prathamesh Gavankar and others have filed a petition before the Bombay High Court challenging changes to form 6 and seeking a judicial probe. But these petitions are not the only challenge to the process. There have been other legal battles over the SIR. One of them, the Bihar SIR challenge, has already been decided. Newslaundry spoke to senior lawyers who represented petitioners in these states, including Prashant Bhushan (represented RTI activists and civil liberty groups in Delhi), Menaka Guruswamy (TMC in West Bengal), Shyam Diwan (Mamata Banerjee), Gopal Sankaranarayanan (electoral transparency outfit ADR) and Abhishek Manu Singhvi (opposition parties and civil society groups). items.title: India’s strategic value cannot rest on US-China hostility
items.summary: After a summit between the leaders of the world’s major powers, the temptation is to read too much into it too soon. At the same time, the turbulence of the international order and the vagaries of geopolitics in recent years have meant that many diplomatic takeaways from such meetings have short shelf lives. Agreements are revised, understandings unravel, and today’s apparent shift in the balance can look rather different after the next crisis, negotiation or election. Therefore, any reading of the Trump-Xi meeting in Washington must be made with a degree of caution. Even after factoring in these uncertainties, a question remains from a distinctly Indian standpoint. What does it mean for New Delhi when Washington and Beijing, the world’s two most powerful states, are trying to recalibrate their relationship and adjust the balance of their rivalry? The question becomes particularly important for India because, on September 12 and 13, New Delhi was itself engaged with Xi Jinping at the BRICS summit, working to protect its interests in a grouping in which China and Russia remain major players. The Trump–Xi meeting needs to be viewed not as an isolated encounter between two great powers, but in light of the choices India has been making at home, in its neighbourhood and across its wider diplomatic relationships. The question would have looked different when Xi was in New Delhi. India was then trying to show that it could work with China and Russia within a larger multilateral framework without turning BRICS into an anti-American bloc. The objective was not to erase disagreements but to prevent disagreements from paralysing cooperation. The same instinct is visible in India’s handling of China bilaterally. The relationship has not returned to the pre-Galwan comfort zone, nor can it be described as a settled partnership. But neither side seems interested in letting every disagreement become a confrontation. The border remains the central security problem while trade imbalance, market access and supply chains remain core economic concerns. Yet political engagement has resumed. Strategic stability, Indian anxiety In some ways, this can be better seen as competitive coexistence than either confrontation or smooth reconciliation. With these elements in play, the Trump-Xi summit adds another layer to this calculation. items.title: Kerala High Court quashes State decision to abolish Kerala Police Officers Association
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday quashed the State government's decision to dissolve the Kerala Police Officers Association (KPOA), as part of its move to restructure associations formed by police officers in Kerala [ Kerala Police Officers Association v State of Kerala & connected cases ]. The State Home Department's order was aimed at reorganising three associations representing different ranks of police personnel. The State's move resulted in the dissolution of one of the three police associations (KPOA), while the remaining two were to be retained in a reorganised form. This was challenged before the High Court by the KPOA. Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas today ruled in KPOA's favour, holding that the State did not have the power to restructure the three police associations in the way it did, that its decision interfered with the constitutional right of the police officers to continue in their associations. "The recognition granted to the members of the police force to form associations has not been revoked either by the State Police Chief or even by the government. Thus under no circumstances could the government have interfered with the structure of the recognized police associations ," it added. The Court further held that the freedom to form associations guaranteed under Article 19(1)(c) of the Constitution is not exhausted once an association is formed, but extends to preserving the association and its composition. " The freedom to form an association and freedom to continue the association are both facets of Article 19(1)(c) of the Constitution, " the Court said. Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas The ruling came on petitions challenging a government order dated July 27, 2026. The order had abolished the KPOA and reorganised the membership of the two remaining bodies - the Kerala Police Association (KPA) and Kerala Police Senior Officers Association (KPSOA). The government order had also directed that the KPOA's assets, including its bank accounts, documents, deposits, investments, rights and liabilities, were to be distributed between the two remaining bodies in a 60:40 ratio. It further stated that ad hoc committees would take over certain administrative duties and that elections to the newly constituted associations would be conducted by September 30. The Court, however, noted today that the State's move conflicted with a proposal made by the State Police Chief himself in January this year. items.title: From 'just one more' to 'buy the whole damn pack': Allahabad High Court judge writes poem on dangers of smoking
items.summary: Justice Shekhar B Saraf of Allahabad High Court has written a poem to highlight the dangers of smoking. Justice Saraf annexed the poem to a judgment delivered by him and Justice Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary on Tuesday on the illegality of serving hookah in the restaurants in Uttar Pradesh . "From my own experience of smoking, I pen these last paragraphs in an attempt to educate the young generation of this country to not become a prey to the deleterious and indelible habit of tobacco smoking," Justice Saraf said. The judge writes that he was an unwilling smoker in the beginning but it soon turned into a habit. "I entered law school pure as morning dew, Sneered at the smokers puffing by the gate, “Weak-willed,” I scoffed, “I’d never join that crew” Famous last words. Reader, I was bait. It started with a ‘chaii’, innocent and warm, A senior offered, “Try one, just for fun.” I took it like a soldier joins a storm Bravely, stupidly, and one by one. The “occasional” ‘sutta’ soon grew bold, It multiplied like rabbits, unrestrained." The judge went on to highlight how smoking became a norm for him. "My lungs, once mine, were quietly sold To a landlord who never once explained the lease. I told myself I merely dabbled, A social smoker, cultured, in control. Meanwhile the count crept steadily From 'just one more' to 'buy the whole damn pack'. Justice Saraf also wrote how smoking badly affected his physical health. "Then came the cough, my body’s stand-up act, Performing nightly, free of charge, unasked. The phlegm arrived, a most unwelcome fact, As if my throat had been recently tasked With hosting a swamp. I tried the patch, it itched. I tried the gum, I chewed it, then lit up regardless, Like a dieter who’s sworn off cake, then switched Straight to the icing, calling it “harmless.” “I’ll quit,” I said, with great conviction twice, Then thrice, then roughly forty times a year. Each January brought the same advice From me, to me, which I did not adhere." Justice Saraf conceded that he has failed to quit smoking despite multiple attempts. items.title: 2021 Antilia bomb scare: Mumbai court grants bail to Sachin Waze, says no evidence Ambani family was terrorised
items.summary: A special National Investigation Agency (NIA) court in Mumbai has granted bail to former police officer Sachin Waze in the 2021 Antilia bomb scare and Mansukh Hiran murder case. Special judge Chakor S Baviskar questioned the applicability of terrorism charges under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). The court found a significant flaw in the prosecution's case regarding the explosives-laden SUV parked near Mukesh Ambani's residence. It noted a complete absence of witness statements from the Ambani family. “The prosecution is not coming up with any specific case that, exactly in whose mind accused Sachin (Waze) wanted to create terror... Even if we suppose on ourselves that, he wanted to create terror in the minds of Ambanis, it is impossible to accept that, any such terror was in fact ever created in the mind of anyone, least in the minds of Ambanis. Because till this moment, there is no statement recorded under section 161 or section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 of any of the family members of the Ambanis, nor of their near and dear relatives,” the judge added. The judge severely criticised the NIA for failing to examine the victims. “Whatsoever the reasons may be for not recording the statements of any of the family members of the Ambanis, it is certainly precarious to the credibility of the prosecution case." The court observed that after the incident, the target and other family members are very much available generally and easily. “Office of the Investigating Agency i.e. of the NIA and the Antilia, i.e. residence of the Ambanis, are literally just wall to wall adjacent!” the judge said. He added that this lapse must be viewed with great pity if it is not outright incompetence. The prosecution alleged that Waze parked an explosive-laden SUV near Mukesh Ambani's residence to extort money and restore his reputation. Subsequent events led to the murder of Mansukh Hiran because he refused to take the blame. The court acknowledged the homicidal death, but concluded that the murder was not a direct outcome of a terrorist act. It highlighted that key co-accused Pradeep Sharma and Sunil Mane had already secured bail. The parity principle heavily favored Waze, who has been incarcerated since his March 2021 arrest. The court ordered Waze to execute a personal bond of ₹1 lakh with a local surety. items.title: Allahabad High Court protects CJP activist from arrest over video of government school
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on September 28 granted interim protection from arrest to Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) member Gaurav Bharti in connection with an first information report (FIR) registered against him for filming the dilapidated condition of a government primary school in Farrukhabad [ Gaurav Bharti @ Gaurav Kumar v. State of U.P. and 3 Others] . A Division Bench comprising Justice Salil Kumar Rai and Padam Narain Mishra issued the direction on petition filed by Bharti seeking the quashing of the criminal proceedings initiated against him. "The petitioner shall not be arrested in pursuance of the First Information Report dated 19.08.2026, registered as Case Crime No. 0246 of 2026, under Sections 352 and 353 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and Section 66 of the Information Technology Act, 2000, Police Station- Nawabganj, District Fatehgarh," the Court directed. The controversy stemmed from an FIR registered on August 19 at Nawabganj Police Station in Fatehgarh district. According to the FIR, the petitioner was accused of having "illegally prepared a video of the institution and had misrepresented the condition of the institution." Bharti recorded the footage as part of the CJP’s ongoing 'School Thik Karo' campaign, an initiative aimed at highlighting poor civic infrastructure and lacking basic facilities in state-run primary schools. Justice Salil Kumar Rai Bharti's counsel contended that the recitals in the FIR were completely baseless and false. It was further argued that in any event, the petitioner could not be prosecuted for the offences in light of an earlier ruling of the High Court delivered this month. The Bench observed that "the matter requires consideration." It noted that the Additional Government Advocate had accepted notice on behalf of the State authorities and directed the issuance of notice to the complainant. The Bench granted eight weeks' time to all respondents to file their counter-affidavits, allowing four weeks thereafter to the petitioner to file a rejoinder. Bharti was granted interim protection from arrest. The matter was directed to be listed following the expiry of the stipulated period. Advocates Ankur Azad, Saumitra Anand, Shashank Tiwari, Shashwat Anand and Shrey represented Bharti. [Read Judgment]

items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday criticized the commercialization of private healthcare, observing that corporate hospitals operate as profit-driven industries rather than service providers while common citizens and taxpayers bear the brunt of exorbitant drug markups [ Kishan Chand Jain v. Union of India ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta noted that corporate hospitals compel admitted patients to purchase medicines exclusively from their in-house pharmacies at inflated retail prices, while patients who bring medicines from outside are left high and dry with hospitals refusing to assure treatment. items.title: Delhi High Court quizzes Meta over Instagram feature being misused to violate copyright
items.summary: The Delhi High Court today raised concerns that a feature on social media platform Instagram could be used as a tool to violate the copyrights of original content creators [ Dr Vikas Divyakirti vs Meta Platforms ]. Addressing counsel representing Meta (which owns Instagram) Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani noted that this feature allows Instagram users to make changes to reels posted by others, and re-upload a modified version. "Tell me Mr Pathak (Meta's counsel), you have a feature on Instagram that you can pick up a video, paste it and make it your own video. For example, someone is cooking a recipe, you can take the whole video and add yourself cooking as per the recipe and run it on your own handle," the Court observed. The Court stated that this Instagram feature allows manipulation and enables copyright infringement. "You are allowing manipulation. It is a tool for copyright violation. Does your platform permit this? It is proof of copyright violation. It is a mischievous feature you have got there. These are powerful tools you are creating; then you give these to a ghost. You don't know who is going to use these tools. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani Advocate Varun Pathak, representing Meta, stated that he will look into the concerns raised by the Court. The Court was possibly referring to Instagram's “remix” feature, which allows users to create a new reel using an existing public reel or video. items.summary: Japanese pharmaceutical company Daiichi Sankyo told the Supreme Court on Tuesday that nearly ten years after securing a foreign arbitral award against former Ranbaxy promoters Malvinder Mohan Singh and Shivinder Mohan Singh, it was still struggling to execute the award [Yes Bank Vs Daiichi Sankyo]. Senior Advocate Arvind Datar , appearing for Daiichi, said the company had pursued arbitration, obtained an award on April 29, 2016 and then initiated execution proceedings, but was yet to realise the award. " It’s 10 years to execute an award, international award ,” Datar said. He added that the situation has become a “spider’s web”, with disputes continuing over what happened to shares of Fortis Healthcare Limited (FHL) held by the judgment debtors. items.title: Non-insurer-insurer mergers: Decoding IRDAI’s new regulation 30A amalgamation framework
items.summary: An insurer may now merge with a non-insurance company, but only within narrow limits. On July 30, 2026 , the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India ( “IRDAI” ) notified amendments to the IRDAI (Registration, Capital Structure, Transfer of Shares and Amalgamation of Insurers) Regulations, 2024 (the “Registration Regulations” ) creating an express pathway for such an amalgamation. The gateway is confined to a holding company whose only business is holding the insurer, with consideration in equity shares alone. This article explains the change, its consequences for transaction design and the questions it leaves open. The amendments followed an exposure draft of 16 June 2026, on which comments closed on 06 July 2026. They operationalised one of the central reforms of the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act, 2025 (the “Amendment Act” ), which is the merger of a non-insurance entity with an insurer. Why Section 35 blocked holding company mergers The lacuna was exposed in 2016–17, when Max Life Insurance Company was to merge into its listed parent, Max Financial Services, as part of the larger HDFC Life transaction. The IRDAI rejected the proposal , holding that Section 35 of the Insurance Act, 1938 ( “Insurance Act” ) contemplated amalgamation only between insurers. Restructurings touching an insurer thereafter kept non-insurance entities outside the perimeter. The issue came up again in IRDAI v. Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd. On March 10, 2025, the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal held that Section 35 does not prohibit an insurer from amalgamating with a non-insurance company under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013 ( “Companies Act” ). In other words, company law allowed what the sectoral regulator had resisted. What the Amendment Act changed In force from February 5, 2026, the Amendment Act rewrote Section 35 to permit a scheme to amalgamate the non-insurance business of any company with the insurance business of an insurer. Section 37, correspondingly, now refers to two or more entities instead of two or more insurers. In doing so, Parliament accepted the result which the Tribunal had reached but handed back to the regulator the gatekeeping role that the ruling had taken away. The change is part of a broader liberalisation that has also raised the foreign investment ceiling up to 100 per cent and the approval threshold for share transfers from 1 to 5 per cent. items.title: No fear of animal cruelty law because of low fines: J&K High Court calls for heavier penalties, jail time
items.summary: The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh recently called for stricter jail time and heavier penalties for offences under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 [Anwar Jan v. Union Territory of J&K] . The Bench observed that animals experience pain, stress and fear like humans, while noting that the existing legal framework continues to treat animals largely as objects or property. It also expressed concern over the penalties prescribed under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, observing that fines for certain acts of cruelty can be as low as ₹10 to ₹50. "Since these fines are so low, there is almost no fear of the law, which is why we see people committing acts of abuse just to post videos on social media for views. While the courts have agreed that animals deserve to live without suffering, the written law has not changed enough yet. For real change to happen, the law needs to officially recognize the animal feelings and replace those tiny fines with strict jail time and heavy penalties,” the Court observed. A Division Bench of Justice Sanjeev Kumar and Justice Mohd Yousuf Wani made the observations while allowing an appeal against the dismissal of a habeas corpus petition filed by Anwar Jan (Choudhary), who had been detained under the Jammu & Kashmir Public Safety Act, 1978. Justice Sanjeev Kumar and Justice Mohd Yousuf Wani The record showed that Jan had been involved in several criminal cases and was also accused in multiple bovine-smuggling cases. He had previously faced PSA detention as well. The Court said that bovine animal smuggling is not merely a criminal offence but can also hurt religious sentiments and has the potential to disturb public tranquillity. However, it clarified that even in such cases, authorities must strictly comply with the constitutional safeguards governing preventive detention. The Division Bench found several serious defects in the latest detention order. It noted that the appellant was already in custody but the detention order did not demonstrate awareness of his custody or record any compelling reason showing a real possibility of his release and subsequent involvement in prejudicial activities. The Court also noted an unexplained 18-day delay between the passing of the detention order on December 1, 2025 and its execution on December 19, 2025. items.title: Rajah & Tann's Ng Kim Beng on the firm's growth story, AI and PE-backed law firms
items.summary: Ng Kim Beng took over as Managing Partner of Rajah & Tann, Singapore a year back. In this conversation with Bar & Bench's Pallavi Saluja, Beng talks about why the firm has grown from just over 30 lawyers to more than 1,100, why India remains part of the firm's vision and why AI's efficiency gains haven't touched the billable hour just yet. He is candid, too, about what worries him: a wave of US firms turning to private equity funding that Asian firms, without similar backing, may struggle to match. [Watch Interview] Edited excerpts follow. Pallavi Saluja (PS): What have been your priorities since you took over as Managing Partner at Rajah & Tann a year ago? Ng Kim Beng (NKB): My predecessor Patrick Ang laid out: people, processes and practice. On people - making sure we continue to attract and retain the right talent and support their growth. One topic that's very current within the firm is the profession's sustainability and, within that, career prospects for younger lawyers. They're often unfairly labelled as a "softer generation," but I think they come with ambition, drive and motivation, on top of the evergreen qualities of diligence and industry. What's changed is a sense of purpose. In my time, that came easily: you joined a good firm, worked under a good mentor, kept your head down and a path more or less opened up for you. That's changed now. The space is far more crowded, competition among peers is sharper, clients are more sophisticated and technology has accelerated all of it. It's about helping them navigate those conditions and helping them see a future for themselves here. On process, the firm has grown enormously since I joined straight out of university, when we had just over 30 lawyers. Today we're 450 fee earners in Singapore and over 1,100 across Southeast Asia. Some of our systems and processes have served us well but are now worn and need upgrading and replacement. We need clearer, more consistent processes and better centralised support, making sure that it is set up in a way that there is a good degree of accessibility. One thing I've learned is that management can end up in a bubble: colleagues out doing hearings and travelling for work don't always know what support is available at HQ. So communicating that accessibility matters just as much as building the systems themselves. Finally, practice is probably the most important of the three, because it's what funds everything else. The company’s case was that it had been using the "Energy Drink" descriptor for its beverage products in India since 2002 and that FSSAI had itself previously recognised its use for the relevant category of caffeinated beverages. Red Bull had also relied on a March 2024 FSSAI advisory which, according to the petition, permitted the expression “Energy Drink” for products falling under the relevant food categories. items.title: Bombay HC asks sessions court to reconsider plea to close POCSO case against accused with mental incapacity
items.summary: The Nagpur bench of the Bombay High Court recently quashed a sessions court order that had refused to discharge a 19-year-old accused in a POCSO case, despite medical evidence establishing his mental incapacity to face criminal trial. Justice Mehroz K Pathan remanded the matter back to the Additional Sessions Court in Bhandara district of Maharashtra for fresh consideration. Justice Mehroz K Pathan The accused faced prosecution for offences under the Indian Penal Code and the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act). His lawyers filed a plea to discharge him from the case, claiming that he suffered from severe intellectual vulnerability. They argued that he could not comprehend his actions or instruct counsel. The High Court was also critical of the sessions judge's failure to record whether there are sufficient grounds to proceed against the accused on merits as per the charge-sheet. items.title: Kunal Kamra moves Supreme Court in 7-judge bench case on limits of legislative privileges
items.summary: Comedian Kunal Kamra has approached the Supreme Court seeking to intervene in a case pending before a seven-judge Bench of the Court on the extent to which an exercise of legislative privileges can be used to curtail a citizen’s freedom of speech. Kamra has sought permission to be made party in the case of N Ravi and ors v. Speaker, Legislative Assembly, Chennai , in which the Court is slated to examine the interplay of legislative privileges with the freedom of speech and the right to life and liberty. Kamra was prompted to move his plea for intervention on account of the breach of privilege proceedings that he presently faces before the Maharashtra assembly over a satirical song played on his comedy show ‘Naya Bharat.’ Kamra’s satirical performance dwelt on the split of the Shiv Sena party in 2022, which led to the resignation of then Chief Minister Uddhav Thackeray, and the eventual formation of a new State regime led by Eknath Shinde. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday asked the Central government to examine whether statutory rules can be put in place to ensure that social media platforms comply with Indian law governing contracts entered into by minors. items.title: Karnataka HC quashes FIR against BJP's Chalavadi Narayanaswamy, TS Srivatsa over remarks about ST status to Kurubas
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has quashed a first information report (FIR) against Karnataka Legislative Council Leader of Opposition T Narayanaswamy alias Chalavadi Narayanaswamy and BJP MLA T S Srivatsa over their statements opposing the proposed grant of Scheduled Tribe (ST) status and reservation to the Kuruba community [T Narayanaswamy @ Chalavadi Narayanaswamy V. State of Karnataka] . By way of an order passed on August 20, Justice M Nagaprasanna held that the allegations in the complaint, even if taken at face value, did not disclose the ingredients of an offence under Section 353(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Justice M Nagaprasanna The Court noted that the petitioners had merely opposed the proposed reservation and held that such opposition, by itself, could not constitute an offence under the provision. "Talks that were going on at that point in time, this by itself would not make an offence under Section 353(2) of the BNS / Section 505 of the IPC" the Court said. The case arose from allegations that Narayanaswamy and Srivatsa had made statements opposing the demand for ST status and reservation for the Kuruba community. According to the prosecution, Narayanaswamy had made the statements from his office, while Srivatsa had made statements in Mysuru and subsequently posted them on social media. It was alleged that while opposing the reservation demand, the BJP leaders had also made statements against the Chief Minister and humiliated members of the Kuruba community. The High Court examined the ingredients of the alleged offence in the light of the Supreme Court's judgments dealing with criminalisation of speech. The bench noted that mens rea is an essential ingredient for an offence relating to promotion of enmity and that allegedly objectionable words have to be assessed in their entirety and in the context in which they were made. The Court also rejected the contention that an FIR cannot be quashed merely because the investigation is at a nascent stage. items.title: Collegium recommends 3 new judges for Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium on Monday recommended the names of 3 High Court Chief Justices for elevation to the apex court. Those recommended to be appointed as judges of the top court are: 1. Justice Sunita Agarwal , Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court. 2. Justice DK Upadhyay , Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court. 3. Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh , Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court. Justice Agarwal, who is originally a judge of the Allahabad High Court, has been the Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court since July 2023. She graduated in law from Awadh University in 1989 and has been in the legal profession since December 1990. She was appointed as a judge in November 2011. Once elevated to the top court, she will retire in April 2031. Justice Singh studied law at the University of Delhi and enrolled as an advocate in 1990. He practiced before the Patna High Court from 1990 to 2000 and then before the Jharkhand High Court till elevation as its judge in 2012. He was the Acting Chief Justice of the High Court from December 20, 2022 and February 19, 2023. He was then elevated as the Chief Justice of the Tripura High Court where he took oath on April 17, 2023. Justice Singh was then transferred to the Telangana High Court where he took oath on July 19, 2025. Justice Upadhyaya studied law at Lucknow University and enrolled as an advocate in May 1991. He remained the Chief Standing Counsel for the State of Uttar Pradesh from May 2007 till his elevation as a judge in November 2011. In July 2023, he was appointed as the Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court. He was then transferred as the Chief Justice of Delhi High Court in January 2025. While its approved strength is 38, the top court currently has 34 judges. items.title: Kerala High Court invokes Mammooty's 1994 movie, says plight of cancer patients remains unchanged
items.summary: The Kerala High Court today invoked Mammotty-starrer ' Sukrutham ', a 1994 malayalam film written by MT Vasudevan Nair, to highlight how the burden of cancer treatment continues to push patients and their families into financial hardships [ In Re Exorbitant Pricing of Life Saving Patented Medicines ] Justice Harisankar V Menon made the observation in an epilogue to a judgment concerning the exorbitant pricing of patented cancer medicine . The film cited by the judge revolves around the character named Ravishankar, played by Mammootty, who is a journalist diagnosed with blood cancer. The movie show his struggles with the prospect of death and the impact of his illness on those around him. Justice Menon particularly referred to a scene in which Mammootty's character tells his doctor that he would not opt for treatment citing the crushing financial burden that cancer treatment places on patients and their families. " He follows this with a heartbreaking monologue on how cancer patients and their bystanders end up pledging their entire lives to afford proper medical care, only to be left buried in mountains of debt, " the judgment said. Justice Menon observed that the situation portrayed in the film continues even today despite the enormous technological advances made since the movie released in 1994. " It is highly distressing that despite the passage of more than three decades since this story was adapted into the movie vocabulary, and won accolades at the National and State levels, and despite the growth of technology, the plight of patients and their families remains the same, " the Judge added. items.title: Sohrabuddin case: Supreme Court says it will not reopen Amit Shah's discharge but seeks CBI reply on plea against acquittal of others
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday issued notice on an appeal challenging the acquittal of all 22 accused, including 21 police personnel, in the case registered on allegations that Sohrabuddin Shaikh, his wife Kauser Bi and associate Tulsiram Prajapati were killed in a fake encounter by the Gujarat police. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought the response of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) which investigated the matter, as well as the 22 persons who were acquitted in the case. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday cancelled the bail granted to Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Mhatre in a case concerning the alleged assault on doctors and hospital staff in Dombivli [ State of Maharashtra v. items.title: Three-language policy: Supreme Court directs CBSE to grant class 6 same exemption allowed to class 7
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) to extend the exemption granted to students of classes VII, VIII and IX under the three-language formula to Class VI students as well [Yashica Bhandari Jain & Ors. v. Union of India & Ors.]. A bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana overruled the Central government’s stand against the exemption. The government had said that nearly 99 percent of schools under the CBSE are ready to implement the policy. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana Under the transitional framework mandated by the Court, students will continue studying the third language as part of their curriculum, but will not face a mandatory class X Board examination in the subject, nor will their final promotion or certification be stalled on account of it. The direction was passed in a batch of petitions filed by parents and teachers challenging a CBSE circular issued on May 15, 2026. The circular had aligned the CBSE scheme of studies with the National Education Policy 2020 (NEP) and the National Curriculum Framework for School Education 2023 (NCF-SE), mandating that students in Classes VI-IX study three languages, including at least two native Indian languages. The petitioners argued that the sudden mandate reversed CBSE’s earlier circular of April 9, 2026, which had deferred the third-language requirement until 2029–30. They contended that introducing the mandate mid-stream caused acute academic disruption as there was a severe deficit of trained language teachers and textbooks. They added that it unfairly prejudiced students preparing for secondary board examinations. While issuing notice in May , the top court had flagged administrative and logistical hurdles over the sudden rollout. items.title: Red Bull moves Delhi High Court challenging FSSAI order to drop ‘Energy Drink’ label
items.summary: Red Bull has moved the Delhi High Court challenging a Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) direction requiring it to discontinue the use of the words “Energy Drink” for its product [ Red Bull Vs UoI ]. The matter came up before Justice Amit Mahajan on Monday, when the Court questioned whether the company had been issued any show-cause notice or given an opportunity of hearing before the FSSAI order was passed. “ If there is no notice… it has to go ,” the Court remarked during the hearing. The Court asked FSSAI to take instructions specifically on whether any notice had been issued to Red Bull before the order was passed. It also questioned whether there was any urgency that justified taking action without first hearing the company. “Nothing emergent in it ,” the Court observed. According to the petition, Red Bull has been sold in India since 2002 under the same descriptor of "Energy Drink." The company has alleged that the June order to discontinue this practice was passed without issuing any show-cause notice or giving it an opportunity of hearing. It has further claimed that the July communication led to enforcement action, including seizure of its products at multiple locations across the country. Red Bull has also questioned what it says is a reversal in FSSAI’s own regulatory position. The company has relied on a March 2024 FSSAI advisory which, according to the petition, clarified that the expression “Energy Drink” was permissible for products licensed under the relevant food categories applicable to caffeinated beverages. It has also pointed to an April 2024 press release issued by the Union Health Ministry, as well as to licences, import clearances and no-objection certificates granted over the years for Red Bull products bearing the same descriptor. items.title: J&K High Court orders action against man who wasted court's time with plea to trace non-existent daughter
items.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court recently ordered that a criminal complaint be filed against a man who was found to have approached the Court in 2023 with a plea to trace the whereabouts of a daughter who did not exist. An inquiry carried on the High Court's directions by the Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) at Rajouri found that the petitioner had created a fictitious daughter and accused others of confining her only to harass them and satisfy his ego and frustration. Whereas the petitioner was given several opportunities to explain his conduct, he was not able to provide any proof that the daughter he referred to in his petition was real. The petitioner, as well as his lawyer, eventually stopped appearing in the case altogether. In an order passed on September 17, Justice Sanjay Dhar observed that the petitioner had given false information not only before the police but also before the High Court, and had engaged a constitutional Court in frivolous proceedings for more than three years. " Petitioner, Tassadaq Hussain, not only misled the police authorities but he had the audacity to mislead the highest constitutional Court of the UT of J&K and Ladakh by engaging the Court in these frivolous proceedings for more than three years, thereby wasting the precious judicial time of this Court, “ the Court observed. Justice Sanjay Dhar The Court added that the petitioner's conduct appeared to constitute criminal offences such as giving false statements on oath and to public authorities and giving false evidence, which are dealt with under Sections 216, 217, 227, 229, 233, 236 and 237 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS). " Such elements need to be taught a lesson so that similar acts are not repeated in future ... He deserves to be prosecuted in accordance with law, " the Court said. For this purpose, the Court proceeded to order its Registrar (Judicial) at Jammu to file a complaint against the petitioner before the CJM at Jammu. The matter concerned Rajouri resident Tassadaq Hussain, who had in 2023 approached the High Court claiming that his daughter, Shabeena Kouser, had been taken away by police officials and was being kept in wrongful confinement. He claimed that his daughter was taken away in June 2023, after the police visited his residence along with a person with whom he had been embroiled in some legal disputes. The police said that they had visited his residence in connection with a criminal case registered against Hussain over some missing goats.

The judge flagged the company's position before the arbitral tribunal. “If that is how you interpreted the KKR promotional activities before the arbitrator, how can we allow you to come and argue before us that the definition of promotional activity must be seen in terms of the contract executed?” asked Justice Bagchi. items.title: Supreme Court sets deadline for ECI to decide TMC name and symbol dispute
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday fixed a deadline for the Election Commission of India (ECI) to decide on which of the two Trinamool Congress (TMC) factions is entitled to use the TMC name and its "flower and grass" symbol. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana today directed both TMC factions to complete pleadings in the matter within four weeks. The ECI has been directed to give its final verdict on the matter within three months after such pleadings are submitted. The ECI's counsel requested that six months be allowed to decide the dispute. However, the Court rejected this request. " Three months is good enough ," said Justice Bagchi today. " It is very difficult," the ECI's counsel persisted. " If some extreme exigency arises, come before us ," the Court replied. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The Court passed the order on a plea by TMC leader Mamata Banerjee challenging the ECI's September 17 interim order freezing the All India Trinamool Congress name and its reserved "flowers and grass" symbol, until it takes a final decision on which of two rival TMC camps is the real TMC. The dispute is tied to an internal split of the TMC, after the BJP won the West Bengal State Assembly elections in May and replaced the TMC-led State regime. Shortly after the poll results, ten TMC Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs), led by incumbent Leader of Opposition Ritabrata Banerjee, rebelled against the party led by Mamata Banerjee and formed a new TMC camp. Presently, the rebel TMC camp identifies itself as AITC-Democratic. The camp led by Banerjee has been dubbed the AITC-Mamata faction. Both TMC factions have claimed that they are the real TMC. This question has been pending before the ECI, which on September 17 decided to freeze the TMC name and symbol until a final decision is made. The ECI's interim arrangement prevents both factions from using the All India Trinamool Congress name and symbol for the upcoming West Bengal Assembly by-elections. items.title: Supreme Court refuses to stay Centre's decision to levy MDR on merchant UPI transactions over ₹2,000
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to stay the Central government's recent decision to levy Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions exceeding ₹2,000 [ Anjan Datta v. Union of India ]. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana however asked the government to submit an affidavit explaining the basis for the new framework. The Court passed the order on Public Interest Litigation (PIL) petition challenging the decision. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana Additional Solicitor General N Venkataraman told the Court person-to-person UPI transfers will remain completely free and around 96 percent of merchant transactions will remain unaffected. Under the announced framework, person-to-person (P2P) transfers and person-to-merchant (P2M) payments up to ₹2,000 remain free. However, a 0.4% MDR applies to P2M payments above ₹2,000, with transactions of ₹75,000 and above capped at ₹300. Specified essential sectors attract a flat ₹5 charge, capital-market payments carry a 0.02% levy and merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh per month remain exempt. The petition before the Court said that despite official assertions that merchants cannot pass these costs to consumers, the fee on qualifying receipts will inevitably enter price structures, reduce working capital, and induce refusal of UPI payments and transaction-splitting among low-margin traders. The petition assailed the proposed MDR framework scheduled to take effect from October 15. It highlighted that while UPI payments above ₹2,000 have been exposed to levies, identical "no-charge" protection continues to be extended to RuPay-powered debit cards without any monetary ceiling. The plea assailed the creation of a nationwide compulsory payment burden without disclosing cost studies, underlying methodology, or enforceable anti-pass-through safeguards. The PIL, filed by advocate Anjan Datta, further contended that thresholds like the ₹2,000 transaction mark and ₹1 lakh monthly receipt ceiling are unsupported by disclosed data. A transaction of ₹2,001 attracts a percentage fee while ₹2,000 does not, creating financial "cliffs" that distort market behaviour and discriminate between similarly situated merchants while favouring very high-value transactions via the cap, it was submitted. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a petition seeking directions to the Speaker of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly to promptly decide on applications filed in July seeking the disqualification of 10 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs). A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana saw no ground to doubt that the Speaker would decide the matter within a reasonable timeline. CJI Kant expressed that it is hopeful that the Speaker will follow the timelines established in previous case laws when it comes to deciding on disqualification petitions. Justice Bagchi added that it may not be appropriate for a court to set deadlines for the Speaker, when courts themselves often take time to decide on cases. " Well, I think we should see the mirror before we give directions. There are so many statutes where the judiciary is required to complete proceedings within a time frame. We are gloriously in breach of those laws and then we direct the speaker," he remarked. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana Justice Joymalya Bagchi We should see the mirror before we give directions. There are so many statutes where the judiciary is required to complete proceedings within a time frame. We are gloriously in breach of those laws. Representing Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay, an MLA of the Mamata Banerjee-led TMC who filed the petition before the Supreme Court, Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal pointed out that in this case, the disqualification applications have been pending before the West Bengal Speaker for nearly 3 months. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday declined to advance the hearing of case concerning the pendency of appeals arising out the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana declined to advance the date of hearing. The request to urgently hear the case was made in view of the October 6 by-polls in Rejinagar and Nandigram assembly constituencies. "These are only by-elections, that’s all," CJI Kant remarked. The SIR appeals are pending before the appellate tribunals appointed on orders of the top court. The counsel who made the request for an urgent hearing of the matter said the case was listed for hearing on September 29 but is now tentatively showing as listed for October 5. "We are seeking urgent directions so that it can be listed before that. There are more than 18,000 appeals pending which have not been disposed of. These people did not take part in the first elections," the counsel said. The counsel added that this will be the second time when people will be missing out on voting. The Court then said the case will be listed on October 5. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana As of August 7, only 2% of the 38 lakh appeals filed by voters excluded from the electoral rolls were decided by appellate tribunals since March 2026. According to a Right to Information (RTI) response from the office of the Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal, of the appeals decided, 75,443 resulted in voters being included in the electoral roll, while 7,339 resulted in exclusion. In other words, 91.13% of the decided appeals resulted in inclusion. These voters were not allowed to cast votes during the West Bengal assembly elections held this year. The RTI response was provided in response to Congress MP Isha Khan Choudhury's application. He had sought information on the appeals arising from the SIR exercise. The response revealed that 37,27,838 appeals, or 97.83% of the total, were still pending, with only 1 in every 46 appeals decided so far. Lakhs of voters in West Bengal were prevented from exercising the right to vote in the recent assembly elections in West Bengal as they stood excluded from the electoral roll after the SIR. items.title: Bombay High Court to hear plea against CEC Gyanesh Kumar on October 22,  says no urgency
items.summary: The Kolhapur Circuit Bench of the Bombay High Court on Monday questioned the urgency for hearing a petition seeking restoration of every voter deleted from the electoral rolls in Maharashtra during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). [Prathamesh Govankar & Ors v. Election Commission of India & Ors] Advocate Asim Sarode for the petitioner sought hearing either today or tomorrow, citing urgency. However, the Bench of Justices Sharmila Deshmukh and Neeraj Dhote questioned why the petition ought to be heard so urgently. "What is urgent about it?" Justices Sharmila Deshmukh and Neeraj Dhote Sarode could not establish the urgency. Accordingly, the Bench listed the petition for October 22. The Bench also questioned what private right was being invoked against the Election Commission of India (ECI). "Is it a PIL? Since it's a writ petition, what private right do you have against the Election Commission?" the bench asked. "We have filed a writ petition on behalf of the citizens who are voters who feel their rights are being infringed, " Sarode responded. The plea has challenged the 14 administrative orders passed by the ECI and Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the last 10 months. The plea by three Maharashtra residents relies on reports by Indian Express that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected to these decisions on 14 occasions. According to the plea, the internal objections concerned voter registration, deletions, software processes and the functioning of Electoral Registration Officers (EROs). The petitioners contend that the Election Commission failed to comply with Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023. They allege that CEC Kumar acted unilaterally and failed to discharge his duties faithfully. The plea also challenges July amendments to Form 6. The petitioners have also sought for a stay on the SIR process in Maharashtra. They have sought postponement of the upcoming assembly elections in SIR-affected states until legally compliant electoral rolls are finalized. Till then, they have sought for directions to constitute a judicial committee, headed by a retired High Court Judge, to probe data deletions and software blockages. items.title: Supreme Court says no punitive action against law student accused of instigating fellow students to join CJP dharna
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday ordered that no punitive action be taken against law student Akshat Tripathi based on a ₹5 lakh bond notice issued to him by Uttar Pradesh (UP) authorities over the Cockroach Janta Party protests. A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the direction after the UP government told the Court today that the notice has been withdrawn. "That being so, it is directed that action, if any, taken in the past pursuant to the notice dated September 4 stands annulled. Consequently, no punitive action of any nature shall be taken against the petitioner," the Court said. By way of background, the notice dated September 4 was issued under Section 130 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) by the Executive Magistrate-Third, Greater Noida. It called upon Tripathi to show cause why he should not be bound under with a personal bond of ₹5 lakh and two sureties of like amount, for allegedly instigating fellow students to join a proposed CJP dharna. The notice came three days after the Supreme Court's September 1 order quashing cases against students who took part in the CJP-led protests against exam paper leaks. Tripathi later also filed an application before the top court alleging that the Uttar Pradesh government misled the court by claiming that it has acted against the Executive Magistrate,. It was his argument that when the matter was mentioned on September 9, the State had informed the Court that action has been taken against the concerned official. Subsequently, an Indian Express report said action was taken not against the Executive Magistrate but only against Sub-Inspector Shiva Pandey whose report formed the basis of the notice. The ACP (Executive Magistrate) who actually issued the notice was not suspended as claimed. This was flagged by Tripathi in his latest application before the Court. When the petition came up for hearing on Monday, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati , appearing for the State authorities, said that the notice dated September 4 has been withdrawn. The Court recorded the same while also adding that no action can be taken against the petitioner on the basis of the notice. items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has questioned a single-judge's order directing a judicial probe into caste discrimination allegations against Dr Deepak Sharma, the Head of the Department of Law, Dr. Rajendra Prasad National Law University, Prayagraj (RPNLU) [ Dr Deepak Sharma v State of UP And 5 Others ]. A Bench of Justice Siddhartha Varma and Justice Kunal Ravi Singh said there was no occasion to order a judicial inquiry when an Equal Opportunity Cell is already in place at the university. "Even if the allegations are of a serious nature, the power of the University to examine such allegations through an appropriately constituted Equal Opportunity Cell ought not to have been taken away, as it is within the domain of the University to look into the welfare of the students and deal with situations as they arise," the Court said. However, considering that the inquiry report was required to be submitted by September 24, the Court said the same be placed before it in a sealed cover on September 29, if it has been already prepared. The order was passed by the division bench on an appeal moved by Dr. Sharma who argued that a probe by judicial officers was not required in the matter since it could have been handled by the Equal Opportunity Cell. The complaint filed on August 20 alleged that Sharma, who belongs to an "upper caste" community, resorted to a stricter evaluation of the victim=student's answer sheets due to his caste. The accused is also alleged to have made comments on multiple occasions regarding the student's caste and the reservation benefits availed by him. On September 16, Justice Vinod Diwakar had asked Judge of Small Causes Court Archana Singh and Chief Judicial Magistrate Arun Kumar Yadava to conduct an inquiry into the allegations levelled by a BA LLB (Hons.) student against Dr. Sharma, who is also the Warden of the Boys' Hostel,. items.summary: The Madras High Court has upheld Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA R Seenivasa Sethupathi’s one-vote victory from the Tiruppattur Assembly constituency by rejecting an election petition filed by Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) leader KR Periyakaruppan challenging the result. Justice GK Ilanthiraiyan allowed an application filed by Sethupathi seeking rejection of Periyakaruppan’s election petition at the threshold. items.title: Government can invoke compulsory licensing under Patents Act to make breast cancer drugs affordable: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Monday suggested that the Central government could invoke its powers under Section 100 of the Patents Act, 1970 (Act), to improve access to heavily priced patented breast cancer medicines [ In Re Exorbitant Pricing of Life Saving Patented Medicines ] Justice Harisankar V Menon , however, left the final decision on this matter to the Central government, terming it a policy decision. "It is for the Central Government to consider whether Section 100 of the (Patents) Act requires to be invoked since ultimately the same is a policy decision, " the Court said. Section 100 allows the central government to authorise the use of patented invention for government purposes, even without the patent holder's consent. The Court observed that Section 100 could be invoked by the government to increase access to expensive medicines for needy patients, on a non-commercial basis. "Section 100 is required to be invoked in circumstances where the Government is required to intervene, such as an instance where the medicine manufactured on the basis of a patent is being sold at an exorbitant price," the Court noted. However, it refrained from directing the government to invoke Section 100 in the present case concerning breast cancer drugs. Instead, it said that the government should collate the required data to examine whether a particular medicine is affordable or not and intervene only if necessary. " It is for the Central Government to consider whether Section 100 requires to be invoked after collecting the necessary statistics ... This is especially so, since this Court is of the opinion that the required data to decide whether the particular medicines in question are affordable or not, has not been brought on record, " the Court held. items.title: Supreme Court initiates suo motu case over rise in rape cases in Delhi
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday took suo motu cognizance of recent rape cases in Delhi-NCR, particularly the recent incident involving a teenager in a public park. A Bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran asked the Court's registry to register a suo motu public interest litigation on the issue and list it for hearing. "One cannot help but draw painful parallels with the 2012 Nirbhaya case, raising the question of whether systemic law-enforcement mechanisms have made any meaningful progress in the decade since then," Justice Pardiwala said. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran According to media reports, a 17-year-old girl was gang-raped on September 21 at Astha Kunj Park near Kalkaji Mandir in southeast Delhi by three men posing as police officers. At least 13 cases of sexual assault have been reported from the national capital this month. The Court observed that the increasing incidents across Delhi-NCR starkly underline a systemic failure on the part of law-enforcement and public administrative authorities to guarantee basic public safety. The right to live with dignity, free from the fear of violence, is an intrinsic facet of the fundamental right to life and personal liberty guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution, the Bench said. It added that public spaces, including parks, roads, buses, metro stations, subways and footbridges, cannot be permitted to become high-risk zones because of inadequate illumination or surveillance, lack of patrolling, or other preventable administrative deficiencies. The Court further said that statements made by public authorities and elected representatives expressing concern over such incidents are understandable but devoid of accountability, such expressions fall short of answering the larger institutional question. "Expressing solidarity is not a solution to this social evil," the Court said. It called for a measurable response and fixing accountability upon the authorities entrusted with the prevention of crime, maintenance of public order and protection of vulnerable persons. items.title: Beyond the 0.4%: What UPI’s new fee means for India’s digital public infrastructure
items.summary: India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) is no longer entirely free; a small transaction fee kicks in on UPI from October 15. This means that if you pay a shop via UPI for any amount more than Rs 2,000, the vendor or the shop will be charged 0.4% of that transaction, which is capped at Rs 300 for large payments. As of now, we are told that the consumers pay nothing. Further, person-to-person transfers are said to be free of charge. Small merchants under a monthly cut-off also are said to stay exempt. The entire conversation is now hinged on whether the shopkeeper will absorb the 0.4%, or will they add it to the consumer's bill? Will the exemption line always hold? Will the country's most-used payment app platforms like Paytm, PhonePe, and Google Pay make money off this rule? These are reasonable questions. But by arguing only about who absorbs the 0.4%, we miss the bigger debate: who gets to charge for a piece of public payment infrastructure, who decided that, and what safeguards exist around that decision. The economic model that is not entirely what it says it is Let us begin by picturing a matchmaking app, a mall, or a card network — basically any business that has two different actors, say buyers and sellers. These actors can charge each side differently for a transaction. This concept has come from economists Jean-Charles Rochet and Jean Tirole (Tirole won the Nobel Prize partly for this work). Card networks provide a simple example. Visa and Mastercard charge merchants a fee, while at the very same time, handing consumers cashback and reward points. The reason is simple: if customers want to use their cards, merchants have a strong reason to accept them too. The same language is now being used to describe UPI's merchant fee. Here, merchants cannot walk away, and consumers are, at least as of now, said to be on the sweet free ride. But there is more to the story. The economic literature on such platforms does not suggest that they should simply be free to charge whatever they want. When merchants cannot easily refuse a payment method because customers demand it, the platform has an incentive to charge them more than would be desirable. That finding became policy. In 2015, the European Union capped card interchange fees at 0.2% for debit cards and 0.3% for credit cards, to stop platforms from over-charging. items.title: ‘Our house was under police siege’: Akash’s father on detention ahead of CM Vijay’s visit
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Ahead of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay’s visit to Madurai on Monday, September 28, the parents of Akash Delison, a victim of custodial torture, were placed under house detention for two days amid concerns that they could disrupt the CM’s convoy. Akash, a 26-year-old Dalit man from the Devendrakula Vellalar community, died on March 8 while undergoing treatment at the Government Rajaji Hospital in the city after allegedly being subjected to police torture. The accused are Inspector Dileepan, Sub-Inspector Guhan and Grade-I Constables S Kaleeswaran, P Mahendran, L Deivendran and B Palaniyappan. The police chargesheet said that the accused had deliberately killed Akash after learning about his Dalit identity. Speaking to TNM, Akash’s father Rajesh Kannan said that police personnel were stationed outside their house for two days ahead of Vijay’s visit. “For the past two days, our house was under police siege. When they tried to detain Lenin from the bus stop yesterday, I staged a protest threatening to self-immolate. Only after my protest did the Superintendent instruct the policemen to detain Lenin at my house,” Rajesh said. Lenin is an activist assisting the family in pursuing the case. According to Rajesh, around 15 police personnel and three police jeeps were stationed outside their house. “They did not allow anyone to leave the house. Only after I pleaded with them saying that I have to run my biryani shop did they allow me alone to operate amidst security. Only at 7 pm did they free us from detention,” he said. Rajesh said the police told him that they had been placed under house detention because they feared the family could disturb the Chief Minister’s programme. CM Vijay had visited Madurai to launch the Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram scheme. Akash’s parents had previously raised black flags against Vijay over the lack of justice in their son’s death. “Why would I protest if my son receives justice?” Rajesh asked. Akash died on March 8 after giving a detailed account of the police torture. His family had initially refused to collect his body, demanding action against the police personnel accused of assaulting him.
